open_points.subject: A03 sandbox network namespace
open_points.text: Rule 1 and required test 10 say the environment has "no network interface but the namespace's own loopback", while the formal invariant says "network(environment) = absent" and K-02 says a function has "no network".
open_points.question: Does the sandbox contain an enabled loopback interface, and if so does "no network" mean only that no non-loopback connectivity is available?
options: Keep an enabled loopback interface but prohibit function socket access and all connectivity outside the namespace
Create the network namespace without even an enabled loopback interface
Permit function code to communicate over loopback within its namespace
open_points.default_guess: Keep the namespace's loopback interface, prohibit socket use by function code, and interpret the invariant as no non-loopback connectivity.

open_points.subject: A16 constant-time token matching
open_points.text: Required test 12 says only "A token is compared in constant time with the owner token and with each agent token." It has no witness or definition of constant time, including treatment of unequal token lengths, iteration over all configured tokens, and early termination after a match.
open_points.question: What exact comparison algorithm and observable verification criterion satisfy constant-time matching for tokens of allowed, possibly unequal lengths?
options: Require a named constant-time primitive for every configured token and prohibit early exit
Require fixed-length token decoding followed by fixed-length constant-time comparison
Compare fixed-size token digests in constant time and always scan the complete token list
Treat source inspection of a designated implementation pattern as sufficient verification
open_points.default_guess: Use a standard constant-time comparison for every configured token, scan the entire token list without early exit, and add a dedicated verification witness.

open_points.subject: A18 atomic publication and store rollback tests
open_points.text: Required tests 2, 3 and 5 remain—"A crash during a value write leaves either no file or the complete file", "A failed store call leaves no partial record", and "A value write whose bytes do not match their digest or size publishes no file; writing equal bytes again leaves the published file unchanged"—but their three verification witness references were removed.
open_points.question: Which executable verification artifacts are responsible for proving each of these crash-atomicity, transaction-rollback and immutable-publication requirements?
options: Restore the three former verification witnesses
Name new fault-injection and filesystem verification witnesses
Declare that these required tests are intentionally deferred to a named later state
open_points.default_guess: Restore dedicated witnesses equivalent to kernel_a18_value_write_atomic_publish, kernel_a18_failed_store_call_writes_nothing and kernel_a18_published_file_digest_never_overwritten.

open_points.subject: A15 spool_file_bytes_max enforcement
open_points.text: Required test 3 now says a function writing one byte over `spool_file_bytes_max` fails "under release v1 already by `output_bytes`, which is lower" while its witness remains `verification:kernel_a15_spool_file_ceiling`.
open_points.question: How is the independent `spool_file_bytes_max` rule verified when every function file large enough to cross it has already crossed the lower `output_bytes` limit, so the stated test cannot distinguish which ceiling caused or enforced the failure?
options: Provide a test configuration or release fixture in which the spool-file ceiling is lower than the output ceiling
Verify the spool-file boundary directly below the function-execution layer
Declare the spool-file ceiling redundant for function outputs and specify which other producer can reach it
Accept that the test verifies only the combined limit rather than the spool-file limit independently
open_points.default_guess: Add a controlled boundary test in which the spool-file ceiling can be crossed without first crossing `output_bytes`, while retaining the release-v1 overlap test.
